hook.en: A coin gives 216 heads in 400 tosses. A survey finds more smokers in one city than another. Claims about percentages are tested with the *large*-sample test for proportions.
hook.kn: ಒಂದು ನಾಣ್ಯ 400 ಚಿಮ್ಮುವಿಕೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ 216 ತಲೆ ನೀಡುತ್ತದೆ. ಒಂದು ನಗರದಲ್ಲಿ ಇನ್ನೊಂದಕ್ಕಿಂತ ಹೆಚ್ಚು ಧೂಮಪಾನಿಗಳು. ಶೇಕಡಾವಾರು ಹೇಳಿಕೆಗಳನ್ನು ಅನುಪಾತಗಳ ದೊಡ್ಡ ಮಾದರಿ ಪರೀಕ್ಷೆಯಿಂದ ಪರೀಕ್ಷಿಸುತ್ತೇವೆ.

title.en: Test the equality of two proportions using the pooled estimate

say.en: A coin gives 216 heads in 400 tosses. A survey finds more smokers in one city than another. Claims about percentages are tested with the large-sample test for proportions. In this lesson: Test a single population proportion.
Test the equality of two proportions using the pooled estimate.
Draw conclusions at 5 percent and 1 percent.

body.en: To test $H_0: P = P_0$ using a large sample with *proportion* $p = x/n$: $Z = \dfrac{p - P_0}{\sqrt{P_0 Q_0 / n}}$, $Q_0 = 1 - P_0$. Equivalently, in terms of the number of successes, $Z = \dfrac{x - nP_0}{\sqrt{nP_0Q_0}}$.
body.kn: H₀: P = P₀ ಪರೀಕ್ಷಿಸಲು Z = (p − P₀)/√(P₀Q₀/n). ಯಶಸ್ಸುಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯಲ್ಲಿ Z = (x − nP₀)/√(nP₀Q₀).

narration.en: To test H_0: P = P_0 using a large sample with proportion p = x/n: Z = dfracp - P_0rootP_0 Q_0 / n, Q_0 = 1 - P_0. Equivalently, in terms of the number of successes, Z = dfracx - nP_0rootnP_0Q_0.
narration.kn: H₀: P = P₀ ಪರೀಕ್ಷಿಸಲು Z = (p − P₀)/√(P₀Q₀/n). ಯಶಸ್ಸುಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯಲ್ಲಿ Z = (x − nP₀)/√(nP₀Q₀).

say.en: To test H 0: P equals P 0 using a large sample with proportion p equals x over n: Z equals dfracp - P 0rootP 0 Q 0 divided by n, Q 0 equals 1 - P 0. Equivalently, in terms of the number of successes, Z equals dfracx - nP 0rootnP 0Q 0. SE uses P 0 from H 0.
say.kn: H 0: P equals P 0 ಪರೀಕ್ಷಿಸಲು Z equals (p - P 0)/ the square root of (P 0Q 0 over n). ಯಶಸ್ಸುಗಳ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆಯಲ್ಲಿ Z equals (x - nP 0)/ the square root of nP 0Q 0.

say.en: p equals x over n.
Same Z for proportion or count.

narration.en: The teacher tests a coin that gave 216 heads in 400 tosses, step by step.

say.en: 400 tosses, 216 heads. Under H nought the coin is fair, so P is one half.
Standard error uses P nought: root of 0.5 times 0.5 over 400, which is 0.025.
Z equals 0.54 minus 0.5 over 0.025, which is 1.6.
1.6 is less than 1.96, so it falls in the acceptance region. The coin may be regarded as fair.

narration.en: Two large samples, say smokers in two cities. Set each sample proportion and size. Under H₀: P₁ = P₂ the samples are pooled, p̂ = (x₁ + x₂)/(n₁ + n₂), and Z = (p₁ − p₂)/√(p̂q̂(1/n₁ + 1/n₂)). Z falls in the red region when the difference is significant at 5%.
narration.kn: ಎರಡು ಅನುಪಾತಗಳ ಹೋಲಿಕೆ. ಸ್ಲೈಡರ್‌ಗಳನ್ನು ಸರಿಸಿ, ಓದುಗಳು ಹೇಗೆ ಬದಲಾಗುತ್ತವೆ ಎಂದು ಗಮನಿಸಿ.

caption.en: Two large samples, say smokers in two cities. Set each sample proportion and size. Under H₀: P₁ = P₂ the samples are pooled, p̂ = (x₁ + x₂)/(n₁ + n₂), and Z = (p₁ − p₂)/√(p̂q̂(1/n₁ + 1/n₂)). Z falls in the red region when the difference is significant at 5%.
caption.kn: ಎರಡು ದೊಡ್ಡ ಮಾದರಿಗಳು, ಉದಾ. ಎರಡು ನಗರಗಳ ಧೂಮಪಾನಿಗಳು. ಪ್ರತಿ ಮಾದರಿ ಅನುಪಾತ ಮತ್ತು ಗಾತ್ರ ನಿಗದಿಪಡಿಸಿ. H₀: P₁ = P₂ ಅಡಿಯಲ್ಲಿ ಮಾದರಿಗಳನ್ನು ಒಟ್ಟುಗೂಡಿಸಲಾಗುತ್ತದೆ. ವ್ಯತ್ಯಾಸ 5% ಮಟ್ಟದಲ್ಲಿ ಮಹತ್ವದ್ದಾದಾಗ Z ಕೆಂಪು ಪ್ರದೇಶದಲ್ಲಿ ಬೀಳುತ್ತದೆ.

tryThis.en: Keep p₁ = 0.30 and p₂ = 0.25 with n = 100 each. Is the difference significant? Now try n = 600 each.
Why can the same difference be significant with large samples and not with small ones?
Make p₁ = p₂. What is Z?

text.en: not significant at 5%: accept H₀ (P₁ = P₂)

say.en: Two large samples, say smokers in two cities. Set each sample proportion and size. Under H 0: P 1 equals P 2 the samples are pooled, p̂ = x 1 plus x 2/n 1 plus n 2, and Z equals (p 1 - p 2)/ the square root of (p̂q̂(1 over n 1 plus 1 over n 2)). Z falls in the red region when the difference is significant at 5 percent.

body.en: To test $H_0: P_1 = P_2$ from two *large samples*, pool them: $\hat{p} = \dfrac{n_1p_1 + n_2p_2}{n_1 + n_2} = \dfrac{x_1 + x_2}{n_1 + n_2}$, $\hat{q} = 1 - \hat{p}$. Then $Z = \dfrac{p_1 - p_2}{\sqrt{\hat{p}\hat{q}\,(1/n_1 + 1/n_2)}}$.
body.kn: H₀: P₁ = P₂ ಗೆ ಸಂಯೋಜಿತ ಅಂದಾಜು p̂ = (x₁ + x₂)/(n₁ + n₂). Z = (p₁ − p₂)/√(p̂q̂(1/n₁ + 1/n₂)).

narration.en: To test H_0: P_1 = P_2 from two large samples, pool them: hatp = dfracn_1p_1 + n_2p_2n_1 + n_2 = dfracx_1 + x_2n_1 + n_2, hatq = 1 - hatp. Then Z = dfracp_1 - p_2roothatphatq,(1/n_1 + 1/n_2).
narration.kn: H₀: P₁ = P₂ ಗೆ ಸಂಯೋಜಿತ ಅಂದಾಜು p̂ = (x₁ + x₂)/(n₁ + n₂). Z = (p₁ − p₂)/√(p̂q̂(1/n₁ + 1/n₂)).

say.en: To test H 0: P 1 equals P 2 from two large samples, pool them: hatp equals dfracn 1p 1 plus n 2p 2n 1 plus n 2 equals dfracx 1 plus x 2n 1 plus n 2, hatq equals 1 - hatp. Then Z equals dfracp 1 - p 2roothatphatq,(1 over n 1 plus 1 over n 2). Pooled p̂ = x 1 plus x 2/n 1 plus n 2.
say.kn: H 0: P 1 equals P 2 ಗೆ ಸಂಯೋಜಿತ ಅಂದಾಜು p̂ = x 1 plus x 2/n 1 plus n 2. Z equals (p 1 - p 2)/ the square root of (p̂q̂(1 over n 1 plus 1 over n 2)).

say.en: SE equals the square root of (p̂q̂(1 over n 1 plus 1 over n 2)).
Large samples on both sides.

problem.en: In a sample of 600 men from city A, 450 are smokers; in 900 men from city B, 450 are smokers. Test at 1% whether the proportions of smokers differ.

narration.en: Let us work this out together. In a sample of 600 men from city A, 450 are smokers; in 900 men from city B, 450 are smokers. Test at 1% whether the proportions of smokers differ.

say.en: Let us work this out together. In a sample of 600 men from city A, 450 are smokers; in 900 men from city B, 450 are smokers. Test at 1 percent whether the proportions of smokers differ.
p 1 equals 0.75, p 2 equals 0.50; p̂ = 900 over 1500 equals 0.6, q̂ = 0.4.
SE equals the square root of (0.6 times 0.4 times (1 over 600 plus 1 over 900)) equals the square root of 0.000667 equals 0.0258.
Z equals 0.25 over 0.0258 is approximately 9.68.
9.68 is greater than 2.58: reject H 0. The proportions differ.
So the answer is Z is approximately 9.68; significant difference.

heading.en: Which P goes in the SE?

body.en: In a test, the SE always uses the value under H₀: P₀ for one proportion, the pooled p̂ for two. The sample p goes only in the numerator.
